R9 Undocumented patterns
**R9. Undocumented patterns.** When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Part 1: `case`
| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `open` \| `closed_fraud` \| `closed_legitimate` \| `escalated` | Where the case stands when your agent stops. `open` means more evidence is still pending |
| `verdict` | `fraud` \| `legitimate` \| `uncertain` | Your conclusion |
| `fraud_probability` | number 0–1 | How likely the flagged activity is fraud. Be honest; this is scored for calibration |
| `pattern` | enum, see below | The fraud pattern you identified, `undocumented` if it matches none of the known ones, or `none` |
| `pattern_description` | string | Required when

Part 2: `sar`
| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | boolean | Whether a suspicious activity report should be filed. Must agree with whether `FILE_REPORT` appears in your final actions |
| `reason` | string | Why file, or why not. Cite the policy rule |
| `narrative` | string | Required when `file` is true. The report itself: **who** (customer, cards, merchants, devices), **what** happened, **when** (dates), **where** (locations, channels), **how** it was carried out, **why** it is suspicious. Six to twelve sentences. This is what a regulator reads |
| `subjects` | list of strings

2. Approval routing
| Route | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `auto` | `ALLOW_TRANSACTION`, `MONITOR_CARD`, `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS`, `WARN_CUSTOMER`, `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER`, `STEP_UP_AUTH`, `GENERATE_REPORT`, `CREATE_CASE`, `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, `CLOSE_NO_FRAUD` |
| `L1` (team lead) | `DECLINE_TRANSACTION`; `BLOCK_CARD` when exposure ≤ $2,500 |
| `L2` (fraud manager) | `BLOCK_CARD` when exposure > $2,500; `BLOCK_ALL_CARDS` always; `FILE_REPORT` always |

The agent recommends. Only `auto` actions may be executed by the agent. `L1` and `L2` actions are recommended with the route stated and wait for

sar.narrative: Between 2016-11-15 and 2016-11-22, card C13487-K1 held under customer C13487 was used for 2 transaction(s) totalling $187.33 that this investigation attributes to a single episode of undocumented coordinated abuse. The transactions are 3460634, 3478561, and the first suspicious one is 3460634. They were online transactions under product code(s) C, billed in region code 191.0, made from device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080. How it was carried out: Device profile SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080 appears on 52 cards across 52 cardholders, marked new on 100% of its transactions and behind an anonymous proxy on 100%; 95 prior confirmed-fraud cases touch cards on this device. The same device profile was used by 19 other card(s) in the same period, including C10326-K1, C08168-K1, C01996-K2, C09975-K1, C02975-K1, C01289-K1 and 13 more, which points to a common actor across cardholders. The bank's detection model scored the flagged transaction 0.05; that score prompted the review and was not relied on as a finding. It is reported because Policy 3a: the case names 19 connected card(s); the activity connects to a shared device profile; the activity connects to another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented, rule R9. Actions recommended: CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST.
